item.title: ‘I was damaged greatly’: Donald Trump seeks $230 million from Justice Department — Will the president decide his own payout?
item.description: President Trump stated his Justice Department might owe him $230 million for past investigations, though he claimed little knowledge of specifics and would donate any payout to charity. He filed multimillion-dollar claims alleging rights violations during probes into Russian interference and the classified documents case.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Paul Ingrassia? Donald Trump's nominee to lead Special Counsel office withdraws over racist texts flap
item.description: President Trump's nominee for federal watchdog, Paul Ingrassia, withdrew his candidacy after "racist and pro-Nazi" texts were leaked. Ingrassia's comments, including disparaging remarks about Martin Luther King Jr. and Asian individuals, led to Republican senators withdrawing their support, forcing his withdrawal from the confirmation hearing.

item.title: Donald Trump pardoned January 6 rioter arrested for threatening to kill Hakeem Jeffries: 'Cannot allow this terrorist to live'
item.description: A New York man, previously pardoned for his role in the January 6th Capitol attack, has been arrested. Christopher Moynihan faces charges for allegedly making death threats against House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries. Investigators revealed text messages indicating intent to harm Jeffries. Moynihan was taken into custody and is currently held on bail.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US Marshal and immigrant shot during ICE operation in South LA; DHS issues statement condemning 'sanctuary politicians'
item.description: A federal operation in South Los Angeles turned violent Tuesday when a US Marshal and an undocumented immigrant, who had previously escaped custody, were shot. The suspect allegedly rammed federal vehicles in an attempt to flee, prompting law enforcement to fire defensive shots. Both individuals sustained non-life-threatening injuries and are hospitalized.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Dan Clancy? Twitch CEO going viral after Emiru safety incident and resurfaced livestream clips
item.description: Twitch CEO Dan Clancy faces scrutiny following a serious safety incident at TwitchCon 2025 where streamer Emiru was attacked. Despite Clancy's promises of improved safety measures and swift action against the perpetrator, many users question Twitch's response speed and Clancy's public conduct, fueled by resurfaced clips and recent livestream appearances.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: 'Knocking on cockpit door': American Airlines flight makes emergency landing after pilots mistake crew for hijackers
item.description: An American Airlines flight bound for Los Angeles made an emergency return to Omaha after pilots mistook cabin crew knocking on the cockpit door for a hijacking attempt. A glitch in the intercom system caused the miscommunication, leading to the safe landing and subsequent apology from the captain. The airport confirmed no security threat.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Stephen Colbert vs Karine Jean-Pierre: Heated clash over Joe Biden’s health — who had the upper hand?
item.description: Stephen Colbert confronted Karine Jean-Pierre on Monday night regarding Joe Biden's mental fitness, citing a stark contrast between the President seen at a March fundraiser and his June debate performance. Jean-Pierre defended Biden's capabilities, admitting disappointment with his debate showing, which Colbert described as 'harrowing,' sparking debate about his suitability for office.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'No American boots on ground in Gaza': JD Vance in Israel; claims US will provide only 'useful coordination'
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance affirmed that American troops will not be deployed to Gaza, reinforcing President Trump's pledge. Vance's visit to Israel aims to bolster the Gaza ceasefire, amid concerns that Prime Minister Netanyahu might abandon the truce. Trump urged Middle Eastern allies to intervene against Hamas if the peace deal collapses, warning of severe consequences.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bad omen? Trump-Putin meet in Budapest on hold; Rubio calls Lavrov
item.description: A US official announced no immediate plans for a meeting between Presidents Trump and Putin, following a call between Secretary Rubio and Foreign Minister Lavrov. The Kremlin also confirmed no precise timeframe for a summit. This comes after Trump previously suggested a meeting in Budapest within two weeks.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Burj Khalifa’s true owner revealed: Who is Mohamed Alabbar, the visionary businessman behind Dubai’s iconic skyscraper
item.description: Mohamed Alabbar built the Burj Khalifa, not the Dubai government. He founded Emaar Properties, which also developed The Dubai Mall and Downtown Dubai. Alabbar's vision transformed Dubai into a global hub. His journey mirrors Dubai's ambitious growth. The tower honors Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Alabbar continues to innovate with ventures like Noon.com and Zand Bank.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Louvre heist: Crime scene footage reveals blowtorch and angle grinder among evidence – Watch
item.description: Four thieves executed a daring daylight heist at Paris's Louvre Museum, stealing eight priceless Napoleonic jewels in just seven minutes. Using a crane and power tools, they breached the Apollo gallery, though they left behind the Regent diamond and Empress Eugénie's crown. The incident has exposed security flaws and prompted calls for reinforcement.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt’s ex-girlfriend accuses him of abuse, stalking, and absolute surveillance
item.description: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt faces accusations of abuse and digital surveillance from his ex-girlfriend, Michelle Ritter. Court filings detail allegations of a "system of total control," including monitoring communications and financial coercion. Schmidt denies the claims, calling them false, as the legal dispute over a failed AI startup and multimillion-dollar settlements continues.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Six years in Dubai: Why this UK expat loved it — and the surprising reason he left
item.description: A reflective Quora post by a long-term Dubai resident has reignited debate on expatriate life in the UAE. The author, a UK-based molecular biologist, described the country’s safety, diversity, and opportunity, but also its limits. He left after six years, citing visa restrictions, rising costs, stalled career growth, and one striking admission: “cheap labour makes you lazy.”
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What happened to Ironmouse’s TwitchCon gifts? Fans furious after staff throw VTuber’s fan gifts in trash
item.description: VTubers faced heartbreak at TwitchCon San Diego as venue staff allegedly discarded fan gifts, mistaking them for security risks. Despite fans adhering to guidelines, cherished presents vanished, leading to public apologies and widespread disappointment. This incident, alongside other security concerns, has sparked doubts about TwitchCon's future for virtual creators and their communities.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: What did Sam Pepper do? Kick streamer banned for injuring an 8-year-old girl in India with a firecracker
item.description: British streamer Sam Pepper is facing backlash after a Diwali fireworks incident in New Delhi allegedly injured a young girl. While live-streaming, Pepper fired a firework towards a group, reportedly hitting a girl and causing a cut above her eyebrow. He has since admitted fault, covered medical costs, and been suspended from Kick.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: 'He’s destroying your house': Hillary Clinton slams Donald Trump over White House demolition for new ballroom
item.description: President Trump's plan for a $250 million private White House ballroom has drawn sharp criticism from Hillary Clinton, who decried the project as a misuse of public property. Demolition has begun on the East Wing, with the massive ballroom slated to accommodate nearly 1,000 guests, dwarfing the current East Room. Despite ongoing construction, formal approval from planning commissions is pending.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
